sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

Merge Strategy.name: Merge Strategy
Merge Strategy.description: Specifies the algorithm used to merge content. The 'Defragment' algorithm combines fragments that are associated by attributes back into a single cohesive FlowFile. The 'Bin-Packing Algorithm' generates a FlowFile populated by arbitrarily chosen FlowFiles

allowableValue.description: Generates 'bins' of FlowFiles and fills each bin as full as possible. FlowFiles are placed into a bin based on their size and optionally their attributes (if the <Correlation Attribute> property is set)

Combines fragments that are associated by attributes back into a single cohesive FlowFile. If using this strategy, all FlowFiles must have the attributes <fragment.identifier>, <fragment.count>, and <fragment.index> or alternatively (for backward compatibility purposes) <segment.identifier>, <segment.count>, and <segment.index>. All FlowFiles with the same value for "fragment.identifier" will be grouped together. All FlowFiles in this group must have the same value for the "fragment.count" attribute. All FlowFiles in this group must have a unique value for the "fragment.index" attribute between 0 and the value of the "fragment.count" attribute.

Merge Format.name: Merge Format
Merge Format.description: Determines the format that will be used to merge the content.

allowableValue.description: A bin of FlowFiles will be combined into a single TAR file. The FlowFiles' <path> attribute will be used to create a directory in the TAR file if the <Keep Paths> property is set to true; otherwise, all FlowFiles will be added at the root of the TAR file. If a FlowFile has an attribute named <tar.permissions> that is 3 characters, each between 0-7, that attribute will be used as the TAR entry's 'mode'.

A bin of FlowFiles will be combined into a single ZIP file. The FlowFiles' <path> attribute will be used to create a directory in the ZIP file if the <Keep Paths> property is set to true; otherwise, all FlowFiles will be added at the root of the ZIP file. The <Compression Level> property indicates the ZIP compression to use.
A bin of FlowFiles will be combined into a single Version 3 FlowFile Stream
A bin of FlowFiles will be combined into a single Version 2 FlowFile Stream
A bin of FlowFiles will be combined into a single Version 1 FlowFile Package
The contents of all FlowFiles will be concatenated together into a single FlowFile
The Avro contents of all FlowFiles will be concatenated together into a single FlowFile

Attribute Strategy.name: Attribute Strategy
Attribute Strategy.description: Determines which FlowFile attributes should be added to the bundle. If 'Keep All Unique Attributes' is selected, any attribute on any FlowFile that gets bundled will be kept unless its value conflicts with the value from another FlowFile. If 'Keep Only Common Attributes' is selected, only the attributes that exist on all FlowFiles in the bundle, with the same value, will be preserved.

allowableValue.description: Any attribute that is not the same on all FlowFiles in a bin will be dropped. Those that are the same across all FlowFiles will be retained.

Any attribute that has the same value for all FlowFiles in a bin, or has no value for a FlowFile, will be kept. For example, if a bin consists of 3 FlowFiles and 2 of them have a value of 'hello' for the 'greeting' attribute and the third FlowFile has no 'greeting' attribute then the outbound FlowFile will get a 'greeting' attribute with the value 'hello'.

Correlation Attribute Name.name: Correlation Attribute Name
Correlation Attribute Name.description: If specified, like FlowFiles will be binned together, where 'like FlowFiles' means FlowFiles that have the same value for this Attribute. If not specified, FlowFiles are bundled by the order in which they are pulled from the queue.

mergecontent-metadata-strategy.name: mergecontent-metadata-strategy
mergecontent-metadata-strategy.description: For FlowFiles whose input format supports metadata (Avro, e.g.), this property determines which metadata should be added to the bundle. If 'Use First Metadata' is selected, the metadata keys/values from the first FlowFile to be bundled will be used. If 'Keep Only Common Metadata' is selected, only the metadata that exists on all FlowFiles in the bundle, with the same value, will be preserved. If 'Ignore Metadata' is selected, no metadata is transferred to the outgoing bundled FlowFile. If 'Do Not Merge Uncommon Metadata' is selected, any FlowFile whose metadata values do not match those of the first bundled FlowFile will not be merged.

allowableValue.description: For any input format that supports metadata (Avro, e.g.), the metadata for the first FlowFile in the bin will be set on the output FlowFile.

For any input format that supports metadata (Avro, e.g.), any FlowFile whose metadata values match those of the first FlowFile, any additional metadata will be dropped but the FlowFile will be merged. Any FlowFile whose metadata values do not match those of the first FlowFile in the bin will not be merged.
For any input format that supports metadata (Avro, e.g.), any FlowFile whose metadata values do not match those of the first FlowFile in the bin will not be merged.
Ignores (does not transfer, compare, etc.) any metadata from a FlowFile whose content supports embedded metadata.

TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet;
INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet 
SELECT
	DATE_FORMAT(r.StartDate,'%Y') AS yearkey,
	r.ResolutionId,
	r.ResolutionGroupId,
	r.Compendium,
	r.DocCode,
	CASE
			WHEN r.Type = 1  THEN 'Chỉ thị'
			WHEN r.Type = 2  THEN 'Nghị quyết'
			WHEN r.Type = 3  THEN 'Công văn'
			WHEN r.Type = 4  THEN 'Kết luận'
			WHEN r.Type = 5  THEN 'Thông báo'
			WHEN r.Type = 6  THEN 'Đề nghị'
			WHEN r.Type = 7  THEN 'Quyết định'
			WHEN r.Type = 8  THEN 'Báo cáo'
			WHEN r.Type = 9  THEN 'Quy định'
			WHEN r.Type = 10 THEN 'Hợp đồng'
			WHEN r.Type = 11 THEN 'Đăng ký'
			WHEN r.Type = 12 THEN 'Biên bản'
			WHEN r.Type = 13 THEN 'Quy trình'
			WHEN r.Type = 14 THEN 'Hướng dẫn'
			WHEN r.Type = 15 THEN 'Kiến nghị'
			WHEN r.Type = 16 THEN 'Thanh tra'
			WHEN r.Type = 17 THEN 'Tờ trình'
			WHEN r.Type = 18 THEN 'Giấy phép'
			WHEN r.Type = 19 THEN 'Giấy mời'
			WHEN r.Type = 20 THEN 'Danh sách'
			WHEN r.Type = 21 THEN 'Kế hoạch'
			WHEN r.Type = 22 THEN 'Chương trình'
			WHEN r.Type = 23 THEN 'Giấy uỷ quyền'
			WHEN r.Type = 24 THEN 'Đề án'
			WHEN r.Type = 25 THEN 'Thông tư'
			WHEN r.Type = 26 THEN 'Quy chế'
			ELSE 'Chưa xác định'
	END AS Kieu,
	s.SectorName AS LinhVuc,
	DATE_FORMAT(r.StartDate,'%d/%m/%Y') AS NgayVanban,
	r.AssignOrganizationName AS CoQuanBanHanh,
	r.CreateUser AS nguoitao_id,
	CASE
			WHEN d.Level = 2 THEN d.DepartmentName
			WHEN d1.Level = 2 THEN d1.DepartmentName
			WHEN d2.Level = 2 THEN d2.DepartmentName
			WHEN d3.Level = 2 THEN d3.DepartmentName
			WHEN d4.Level = 2 THEN d4.DepartmentName
			ELSE NULL
	END AS loaicapcha,
	CASE
			WHEN d.Level = 3 THEN d.DepartmentName
			WHEN d1.Level = 3 THEN d1.DepartmentName
			WHEN d2.Level = 3 THEN d2.DepartmentName
			WHEN d3.Level = 3 THEN d3.DepartmentName
			WHEN d4.Level = 3 THEN d4.DepartmentName
			ELSE NULL
	END AS loaicap,
	u.Username AS nguoitao_taikhoan,
	u.FullName AS nguoitao_ten,
	d.DepartmentId AS iddv,
	d.DepartmentName AS donvi,
	IFNULL(d.DepartmentShortName ,'Chưa xác định')  AS tenviettat,
	COUNT(t.TaskId) AS so_nhiem_vu
FROM
	db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution r
	LEFT JOIN egov_hanoi.`user` u ON r.CreateUser = u.UserId
	LEFT JOIN egov_hanoi.user_department_jobtitles_position udjp ON u.UserId = udjp.UserId
	LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d ON d.DepartmentId = udjp.DepartmentId
	LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d1
			ON d1.DepartmentId = d.ParentId
	/* Cha */
	LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d2
			ON d2.DepartmentId = d1.ParentId
	/* Ông */
	LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d3
			ON d3.DepartmentId = d2.ParentId
	/* Cụ */
	LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d4
			ON d4.DepartmentId = d3.ParentId
	LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task t ON t.ResolutionId = r.ResolutionId
	LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_sector s
         ON s.SectorId = r.SectorId
  LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution_group rg
         ON r.ResolutionGroupId = rg.ResolutionGroupId
	LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution_group rg1 ON rg1.ResolutionGroupId = rg.ParentGroupId 
	AND rg1.IsRoot = 0 -- mức 2: cha của cha
	LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution_group rg2 ON rg2.ResolutionGroupId = rg1.ParentGroupId 
	AND rg2.IsRoot = 0 -- mức 3: cha của cha
	LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution_group rg3 ON rg3.ResolutionGroupId = rg2.ParentGroupId 
	AND rg3.IsRoot = 0 -- mức 4: cha của cha
	LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution_group rg4 ON rg4.ResolutionGroupId = rg3.ParentGroupId 
	AND rg4.IsRoot = 0
WHERE d.DepartmentId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
	r.ResolutionId,
	r.ResolutionGroupId,
	r.Compendium,
	r.DocCode,
	r.Type,
	s.SectorName,
	r.StartDate,
	r.CreateUser,
	u.Username,
	u.FullName,
	d.DepartmentId,
	d.DepartmentName
;

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

File Size.name: File Size
File Size.description: The size of the file that will be used

Batch Size.name: Batch Size
Batch Size.description: The number of FlowFiles to be transferred in each invocation

Data Format.name: Data Format
Data Format.description: Specifies whether the data should be Text or Binary

Unique FlowFiles.name: Unique FlowFiles
Unique FlowFiles.description: If true, each FlowFile that is generated will be unique. If false, a random value will be generated and all FlowFiles will get the same content but this offers much higher throughput

generate-ff-custom-text.name: generate-ff-custom-text
generate-ff-custom-text.description: If Data Format is text and if Unique FlowFiles is false, then this custom text will be used as content of the generated FlowFiles and the File Size will be ignored. Finally, if Expression Language is used, evaluation will be performed only once per batch of generated FlowFiles

character-set.name: character-set
character-set.description: Specifies the character set to use when writing the bytes of Custom Text to a flow file.

mime-type.name: mime-type
mime-type.description: Specifies the value to set for the "mime.type" attribute.

relationships.name: failure
relationships.description: SQL query execution failed. Incoming FlowFile will be penalized and routed to this relationship

relationships.name: success
relationships.description: Successfully created FlowFile from SQL query result set.

properties.SQL select query:
/* [RT 12/11 full] ghi *_new_rt; TRUNCATE+INSERT → staging + RENAME swap */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__stg LIKE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt;
TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__stg;
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;
INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__stg
SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT
        DATE_FORMAT(r.StartDate,'%Y') AS yearkey,
        r.ResolutionId,
        r.ResolutionGroupId,
        r.Compendium,
        r.DocCode,
        CASE
            WHEN r.Type = 1  THEN 'Chỉ thị'
            WHEN r.Type = 2  THEN 'Nghị quyết'
            WHEN r.Type = 3  THEN 'Công văn'
            WHEN r.Type = 4  THEN 'Kết luận'
            WHEN r.Type = 5  THEN 'Thông báo'
            WHEN r.Type = 6  THEN 'Đề nghị'
            WHEN r.Type = 7  THEN 'Quyết định'
            WHEN r.Type = 8  THEN 'Báo cáo'
            WHEN r.Type = 9  THEN 'Quy định'
            WHEN r.Type = 10 THEN 'Hợp đồng'
            WHEN r.Type = 11 THEN 'Đăng ký'
            WHEN r.Type = 12 THEN 'Biên bản'
            WHEN r.Type = 13 THEN 'Quy trình'
            WHEN r.Type = 14 THEN 'Hướng dẫn'
            WHEN r.Type = 15 THEN 'Kiến nghị'
            WHEN r.Type = 16 THEN 'Thanh tra'
            WHEN r.Type = 17 THEN 'Tờ trình'
            WHEN r.Type = 18 THEN 'Giấy phép'
            WHEN r.Type = 19 THEN 'Giấy mời'
            WHEN r.Type = 20 THEN 'Danh sách'
            WHEN r.Type = 21 THEN 'Kế hoạch'
            WHEN r.Type = 22 THEN 'Chương trình'
            WHEN r.Type = 23 THEN 'Giấy uỷ quyền'
            WHEN r.Type = 24 THEN 'Đề án'
            WHEN r.Type = 25 THEN 'Thông tư'
            WHEN r.Type = 26 THEN 'Quy chế'
            ELSE 'Chưa xác định'
        END AS Kieu,
        s.SectorName AS LinhVuc,
        DATE_FORMAT(r.StartDate,'%d/%m/%Y') AS NgayVanban,
        r.AssignOrganizationName AS CoQuanBanHanh,
        CASE
            WHEN d.Level  = 2 THEN d.DepartmentName
            WHEN d1.Level = 2 THEN d1.DepartmentName
            WHEN d2.Level = 2 THEN d2.DepartmentName
            WHEN d3.Level = 2 THEN d3.DepartmentName
            WHEN d4.Level = 2 THEN d4.DepartmentName
            ELSE NULL
        END AS loaicapcha,
        CASE
            WHEN d.Level  = 3 THEN d.DepartmentName
            WHEN d1.Level = 3 THEN d1.DepartmentName
            WHEN d2.Level = 3 THEN d2.DepartmentName
            WHEN d3.Level = 3 THEN d3.DepartmentName
            WHEN d4.Level = 3 THEN d4.DepartmentName
            ELSE NULL
        END AS loaicap,
        d.ParentId        AS iddv_captren,
        d.DepartmentId    AS iddv,
        d.DepartmentName  AS donvi,
        IFNULL(d.DepartmentShortName, 'Chưa xác định') AS tenviettat,
        r.CreateUser          AS nguoitao_id,
        u.eGovUserLabel       AS nguoitao_taikhoan,
        u.eGovUserFullname    AS nguoitao_ten,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t.TaskId) AS so_nhiem_vu
    FROM
        (SELECT * FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution WHERE DeletedDate IS NULL) r
        LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_user u ON r.CreateUser = u.eGovUserId
        LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d ON d.DepartmentIdExt = u.DepartmentPath
        LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d1 ON d1.DepartmentId = d.ParentId
        LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d2 ON d2.DepartmentId = d1.ParentId
        LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d3 ON d3.DepartmentId = d2.ParentId
        LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.department d4 ON d4.DepartmentId = d3.ParentId
        LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task WHERE Status <> 5 AND DeletedDate IS NULL) t ON t.ResolutionId = r.ResolutionId
        LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_sector s ON s.SectorId = r.SectorId
    WHERE d.DepartmentId IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
        r.ResolutionId,
        r.ResolutionGroupId,
        r.Compendium,
        r.DocCode,
        r.Type,
        s.SectorName,
        r.StartDate,
        r.CreateUser,
        u.eGovUserLabel,
        u.eGovUserFullname,
        d.DepartmentId,
        d.DepartmentName
) main
WHERE main.loaicap = 'Văn phòng UBND TP'
;
/* đổi chỗ nguyên tử, chờ khóa tối đa 10s */
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 10;
RENAME TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt TO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__old, datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__stg TO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt, datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__old TO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_vanban_chitiet_new_rt__stg;
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 31536000;

TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_donvi_quahan;
INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_donvi_quahan
SELECT
    LEFT(g.monthkey,4) AS yearkey,
    g.loaicapcha,
    g.loaicap,
    g.iddv,
    g.donvi,
    g.tenviettat,
		g.iddv_captren,

    g.loaicapcha_dvthuchien,
    g.loaicap_dvthuchien,
    g.iddv_dvthuchien,
    g.donvi_dvthuchien,
    g.tenviettat_dvthuchien,
		g.iddv_captren_dvthuchien,

    g.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    g.LinhVuc,
    g.Kieu,
    g.UuTien,

    COUNT(*) AS tongso,

    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai LIKE 'Đã hoàn thành%' THEN 1 END) AS daht,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn' THEN 1 END) AS daht_dh,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn' THEN 1 END) AS daht_qh,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành không hạn' THEN 1 END) AS daht_kh,

    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai LIKE 'Chưa hoàn thành%' THEN 1 END) AS dangth,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn' THEN 1 END) AS dangth_th,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn' THEN 1 END) AS dangth_qh,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn' THEN 1 END) AS dangth_sqh,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN g.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành không hạn' THEN 1 END) AS dangth_kh,

    SUM(g.tongtg_canxuly) AS tongtg_canxuly,
    SUM(g.tongtg_daxuly) AS tongtg_daxuly,

    /* số ngày quá hạn lớn nhất */
    qh.songayquahan_max AS songayquahan,

    /* thông tin nhiệm vụ có quá hạn lớn nhất */
    qh.Ma,
    qh.TenNhiemVu,
    qh.SanPhamChuYeu,
    qh.ThoiHanHoanThanh,
    qh.NgayHoanThanh,
    qh.TrangThai,
    qh.TienDoHoanThanh,
    qh.nhomvb_ma,
    qh.nhomvb,

    COALESCE(rpt.SoLanYeuCauBCTD, 0) AS SoLanYeuCauBCTD,
    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_giaonv g

/* ===== lấy nhiệm vụ quá hạn lớn nhất ===== */
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        LEFT(g1.monthkey,4) AS yearkey,
        g1.iddv,
        g1.iddv_dvthuchien,

        mx.songayquahan_max,

        g1.songayquahan,
        g1.Ma,
        g1.TenNhiemVu,
        g1.SanPhamChuYeu,
        g1.ThoiHanHoanThanh,
        g1.NgayHoanThanh,
        g1.TrangThai,
        g1.TienDoHoanThanh,
        g1.nhomvb_ma,
        g1.nhomvb
    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_giaonv g1
    INNER JOIN (
        SELECT
            LEFT(monthkey,4) AS yearkey,
            iddv,
            iddv_dvthuchien,
            MAX(songayquahan) AS songayquahan_max
        FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_giaonv
        WHERE TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn'
        GROUP BY
            LEFT(monthkey,4),
            iddv,
            iddv_dvthuchien
    ) mx
        ON  LEFT(g1.monthkey,4) = mx.yearkey
        AND g1.iddv = mx.iddv
        AND g1.iddv_dvthuchien = mx.iddv_dvthuchien
        AND g1.songayquahan = mx.songayquahan_max
    WHERE g1.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn'
) qh
    ON  LEFT(g.monthkey,4) = qh.yearkey
    AND g.iddv = qh.iddv
    AND g.iddv_dvthuchien = qh.iddv_dvthuchien

/* ===== JOIN báo cáo ===== */
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        TaskId,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN Type = 0 THEN 1 END) AS SoLanYeuCauBCTD
    FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_report
    GROUP BY TaskId
) rpt
    ON rpt.TaskId = qh.Ma

GROUP BY
    LEFT(g.monthkey,4),
    g.loaicapcha,
    g.loaicap,
    g.iddv,
    g.donvi,
    g.tenviettat,
		g.iddv_captren,
    g.loaicapcha_dvthuchien,
    g.loaicap_dvthuchien,
    g.iddv_dvthuchien,
    g.donvi_dvthuchien,
    g.tenviettat_dvthuchien,
		g.iddv_captren_dvthuchien,
    g.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    g.LinhVuc,
    g.Kieu,
    g.UuTien,
    qh.songayquahan_max,
    qh.Ma,
    qh.TenNhiemVu,
    qh.SanPhamChuYeu,
    qh.ThoiHanHoanThanh,
    qh.NgayHoanThanh,
    qh.TrangThai,
    qh.TienDoHoanThanh,
    qh.nhomvb_ma,
    qh.nhomvb
;

Database Connection Pooling Service.name: Database Connection Pooling Service

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

File Size.name: File Size
File Size.description: The size of the file that will be used

Batch Size.name: Batch Size
Batch Size.description: The number of FlowFiles to be transferred in each invocation

Data Format.name: Data Format
Data Format.description: Specifies whether the data should be Text or Binary

Unique FlowFiles.name: Unique FlowFiles
Unique FlowFiles.description: If true, each FlowFile that is generated will be unique. If false, a random value will be generated and all FlowFiles will get the same content but this offers much higher throughput

generate-ff-custom-text.name: generate-ff-custom-text
generate-ff-custom-text.description: If Data Format is text and if Unique FlowFiles is false, then this custom text will be used as content of the generated FlowFiles and the File Size will be ignored. Finally, if Expression Language is used, evaluation will be performed only once per batch of generated FlowFiles

character-set.name: character-set
character-set.description: Specifies the character set to use when writing the bytes of Custom Text to a flow file.

mime-type.name: mime-type
mime-type.description: Specifies the value to set for the "mime.type" attribute.

relationships.name: failure
relationships.description: SQL query execution failed. Incoming FlowFile will be penalized and routed to this relationship

)

		t.`date`,
    t.`month`,
		t.`year`,
    t.nhomvb_ma,

    t.donvi             AS donvi_dvgiao,
    t.tenviettat        AS tenviettat_dvgiao,
    t.NguoiGiaoNhiemVu,

    NULL AS don_vi_cap_01_dvthuchien,
    NULL AS loaicapcha_dvthuchien,
    NULL AS loaicap_dvthuchien,
    NULL AS iddv_dvthuchien,

        WHEN d1.Level = 3 THEN d1.DepartmentName
        WHEN d2.Level = 3 THEN d2.DepartmentName

    '${sync_ts}'     AS syncdate

    ON d2.DepartmentId = d1.ParentId

    t.tenviettat_dvgiao,
    t.NguoiGiaoNhiemVu,

    -- đơn vị thực hiện = đơn vị hiện tại

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

relationships.description: Successfully created FlowFile from SQL query result set.

TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan;

INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan
SELECT
    t.monthkey,
    t.loaicapcha,
    t.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    t.LinhVuc,
    t.Kieu,
		t.UuTien,

    /* Tổng số nhiệm vụ */
    COUNT(*) AS tongso,

    /* ===== ĐÃ HOÀN THÀNH ===== */
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Đã hoàn thành%' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_dh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_qh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành không hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_kh,

    /* ===== CHƯA HOÀN THÀNH ===== */
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Chưa hoàn thành%' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_th,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_qh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_sqh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành không hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_kh,
		SUM(t.tongtg_canxuly) AS tongtg_canxuly,
		SUM(t.tongtg_daxuly) AS tongtg_daxuly,

    t.nhomvb_ma,
    t.nhomvb,
		t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
    t.NhomGiaoNhan,
    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet t
WHERE NOT (
    t.loaicapcha = 'Thành ủy Hà Nội'
    AND t.NhomGiaoNhan = 'Được giao'
) 
/*AND NOT ( t.loaicapcha = 'UBND Thành phố'
    AND 
         t.NhomGiaoNhan = 'Được giao'
          AND t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu = 'Nhiệm vụ nội bộ')*/
GROUP BY
    t.monthkey,
    t.loaicapcha,
    t.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    t.LinhVuc,
    t.Kieu,
		t.UuTien,
    t.nhomvb_ma,
    t.nhomvb,
		t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
    t.NhomGiaoNhan

		
UNION ALL

SELECT
 t.monthkey,

"Thành ủy Hà Nội" AS loaicapcha,

 t.loai_nhiem_vu_viettat AS VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
NULL AS LinhVuc,
NULL AS Kieu,
NULL AS UuTien,
SUM( t.tong_so_nhiem_vu) AS tongso,
SUM( t.da_hoan_thanh) AS daht,
SUM( t.da_hoan_thanh_dung_han) AS daht_dh,
SUM( t.da_hoan_thanh_qua_han) AS daht_qh,
0 AS daht_kh,
SUM( t.on_dinh_dung_han) + SUM( t.thuong_xuyen) + SUM( t.dang_tien_hanh_qua_han) AS dangth,
SUM( t.on_dinh_dung_han) + SUM( t.thuong_xuyen) AS dangth_th,
SUM( t.dang_tien_hanh_qua_han) AS dangth_qh,
SUM( t.sap_den_han) AS dangth_sqh,
0 AS dangth_kh,
NULL AS tongtg_canxuly,
NULL AS tongtg_daxuly,
t.nhom_nhiem_vu AS nhomvb_ma,
t.nhom_nhiem_vu AS nhomvb,
'Nhiệm vụ ngoài khối' AS NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
'Được giao' AS NhomGiaoNhan,
MAX( t.syncdate)
FROM datamart_hanoi.tla_bao_cao_tong_quan t
WHERE t.monthkey = (
    SELECT MAX(monthkey)
    FROM datamart_hanoi.tla_bao_cao_tong_quan
)
GROUP BY 
 t.monthkey,
 t.loai_nhiem_vu_viettat,
 t.nhom_nhiem_vu
		
ORDER BY 
    monthkey,
    loaicapcha,
    VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    LinhVuc,
    Kieu,
		UuTien,
    nhomvb_ma,
    nhomvb,
		NhomGiaoNhan,
		NhomPhamViNhiemVu

Database Connection Pooling Service.name: Database Connection Pooling Service
Database Connection Pooling Service.description: The Controller Service that is used to obtain connection to database

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

relationships.name: failure
relationships.description: SQL query execution failed. Incoming FlowFile will be penalized and routed to this relationship

relationships.name: success
relationships.description: Successfully created FlowFile from SQL query result set.

properties.SQL select query:
TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_btctw;
INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_btctw

SELECT
    t.monthkey,
		t.`year`,
		t.don_vi_cap_01,
    t.loaicapcha,
    t.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
		t.NgayVanBan,
    t.LinhVuc,
    t.Kieu,
		t.UuTien,

    /* Tổng số nhiệm vụ */
    COUNT(*) AS tongso,

    /* ===== ĐÃ HOÀN THÀNH ===== */
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Đã hoàn thành%' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_dh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_qh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành không hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_kh,

    /* ===== CHƯA HOÀN THÀNH ===== */
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Chưa hoàn thành%' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_th,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_qh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_sqh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành không hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_kh,
		SUM(t.tongtg_canxuly) AS tongtg_canxuly,
		SUM(t.tongtg_daxuly) AS tongtg_daxuly,

    t.nhomvb_ma,
    t.nhomvb,
		t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
    t.NhomGiaoNhan,
    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_khoi_btctw t
GROUP BY
    t.monthkey,
		t.don_vi_cap_01,
    t.loaicapcha,
    t.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    t.LinhVuc,
    t.Kieu,
		t.UuTien,
    t.nhomvb_ma,
    t.nhomvb,
		t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
    t.NhomGiaoNhan
;

properties.SQL select query:
/* [RT 12/11] staging + RENAME swap: IOC không bao giờ thấy bảng rỗng/đang sửa dở */
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__stg LIKE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt;
TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__stg;
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;
INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__stg

SELECT
    t.monthkey,
		t.`year`,
		t.don_vi_cap_01,
    t.loaicapcha,
    t.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
		t.NgayVanBan,
    t.LinhVuc,
    t.Kieu,
		t.UuTien,

    /* Tổng số nhiệm vụ */
    COUNT(*) AS tongso,

    /* ===== ĐÃ HOÀN THÀNH ===== */
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Đã hoàn thành%' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_dh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_qh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành không hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS daht_kh,

    /* ===== CHƯA HOÀN THÀNH ===== */
    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Chưa hoàn thành%' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_th,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_qh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_sqh,

    SUM(
        CASE 
            WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành không hạn' 
            THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END
    ) AS dangth_kh,
		SUM(t.tongtg_canxuly) AS tongtg_canxuly,
		SUM(t.tongtg_daxuly) AS tongtg_daxuly,

    t.nhomvb_ma,
    t.nhomvb,
		t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
    t.NhomGiaoNhan,
    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_khoi_new_rt t
WHERE NOT ( t.NhomGiaoNhan = 'Được giao' AND t.loaicapcha = "Thành ủy Hà Nội")
GROUP BY
    t.monthkey,
		t.don_vi_cap_01,
    t.loaicapcha,
    t.VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    t.LinhVuc,
    t.Kieu,
		t.UuTien,
    t.nhomvb_ma,
    t.nhomvb,
		t.NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
    t.NhomGiaoNhan

		
UNION ALL

SELECT
 t.monthkey,
 LEFT(t.monthkey,4) `year`,
 "THÀNH PHỐ HÀ NỘI" AS don_vi_cap_01,
 "Thành ủy Hà Nội" AS loaicapcha,

 t.loai_nhiem_vu_viettat AS VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
 NULL AS NgayVanBan,
'Chưa xác định' AS LinhVuc,
'Chưa xác định' AS Kieu,
'Chưa xác định' AS UuTien,
SUM( t.tong_so_nhiem_vu) AS tongso,
SUM( t.da_hoan_thanh) AS daht,
SUM( t.da_hoan_thanh_dung_han) AS daht_dh,
SUM( t.da_hoan_thanh_qua_han) AS daht_qh,
0 AS daht_kh,
SUM( t.on_dinh_dung_han) + SUM( t.thuong_xuyen) + SUM( t.dang_tien_hanh_qua_han) AS dangth,
SUM( t.on_dinh_dung_han) + SUM( t.thuong_xuyen) AS dangth_th,
SUM( t.dang_tien_hanh_qua_han) AS dangth_qh,
SUM( t.sap_den_han) AS dangth_sqh,
0 AS dangth_kh,
NULL AS tongtg_canxuly,
NULL AS tongtg_daxuly,
t.nhom_nhiem_vu AS nhomvb_ma,
CONCAT('Nghị quyết ',LEFT(t.nhom_nhiem_vu,2)) AS nhomvb,
'Nhiệm vụ ngoài khối' AS NhomPhamViNhiemVu,
'Được giao' AS NhomGiaoNhan,
MAX( t.syncdate)
FROM datamart_hanoi.tla_bao_cao_tong_quan t
WHERE t.monthkey IN (
    SELECT MAX(t1.monthkey)
    FROM datamart_hanoi.tla_bao_cao_tong_quan t1
		GROUP BY LEFT(t1.monthkey, 4)
)
GROUP BY 
 t.monthkey,
 t.loai_nhiem_vu_viettat,
 t.nhom_nhiem_vu
		
ORDER BY 
    monthkey,
		don_vi_cap_01,
    loaicapcha,
    VanBanGiaoNhiemVu,
    LinhVuc,
    Kieu,
		UuTien,
    nhomvb_ma,
    nhomvb,
		NhomGiaoNhan,
		NhomPhamViNhiemVu
;
/* Đổi chỗ nguyên tử; chờ khóa tối đa 10s để không chặn dashboard */
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 10;
RENAME TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt TO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__old, datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__stg TO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt, datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__old TO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tongquan_new_rt__stg;
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 31536000;

Database Connection Pooling Service.name: Database Connection Pooling Service
Database Connection Pooling Service.description: The Controller Service that is used to obtain connection to database

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

put-db-record-record-reader.name: put-db-record-record-reader
put-db-record-record-reader.description: Specifies the Controller Service to use for parsing incoming data and determining the data's schema.

db-type.name: db-type
db-type.description: The type/flavor of database, used for generating database-specific code. In many cases the Generic type should suffice, but some databases (such as Oracle) require custom SQL clauses.

allowableValue.description: Generates ANSI SQL
Generates Oracle compliant SQL
Generates Oracle compliant SQL for version 12 or greater
Generates MS SQL Compatible SQL, for version 2012 or greater
Generates MS SQL Compatible SQL for version 2008
Generates MySQL compatible SQL
Generates PostgreSQL compatible SQL
Generates Phoenix compliant SQL

put-db-record-statement-type.name: put-db-record-statement-type
put-db-record-statement-type.description: Specifies the type of SQL Statement to generate. Please refer to the database documentation for a description of the behavior of each operation. Please note that some Database Types may not support certain Statement Types. If 'Use statement.type Attribute' is chosen, then the value is taken from the statement.type attribute in the FlowFile. The 'Use statement.type Attribute' option is the only one that allows the 'SQL' statement type. If 'SQL' is specified, the value of the field specified by the 'Field Containing SQL' property is expected to be a valid SQL statement on the target database, and will be executed as-is.

Statement Type Record Path.name: Statement Type Record Path
Statement Type Record Path.description: Specifies a RecordPath to evaluate against each Record in order to determine the Statement Type. The RecordPath should equate to either INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, or DELETE.

Data Record Path.name: Data Record Path
Data Record Path.description: If specified, this property denotes a RecordPath that will be evaluated against each incoming Record and the Record that results from evaluating the RecordPath will be sent to the database instead of sending the entire incoming Record. If not specified, the entire incoming Record will be published to the database.

put-db-record-dcbp-service.name: put-db-record-dcbp-service
put-db-record-dcbp-service.description: The Controller Service that is used to obtain a connection to the database for sending records.

put-db-record-catalog-name.name: put-db-record-catalog-name
put-db-record-catalog-name.description: The name of the catalog that the statement should update. This may not apply for the database that you are updating. In this case, leave the field empty. Note that if the property is set and the database is case-sensitive, the catalog name must match the database's catalog name exactly.

put-db-record-schema-name.name: put-db-record-schema-name
put-db-record-schema-name.description: The name of the schema that the table belongs to. This may not apply for the database that you are updating. In this case, leave the field empty. Note that if the property is set and the database is case-sensitive, the schema name must match the database's schema name exactly.

put-db-record-table-name.name: put-db-record-table-name
put-db-record-table-name.description: The name of the table that the statement should affect. Note that if the database is case-sensitive, the table name must match the database's table name exactly.

put-db-record-binary-format.name: put-db-record-binary-format
put-db-record-binary-format.description: The format to be applied when decoding string values to binary.

allowableValue.description: String values for binary columns contain the original value as text via UTF-8 character encoding
String values for binary columns contain the original value in hexadecimal format
String values for binary columns contain the original value in Base64 encoded format

put-db-record-translate-field-names.name: put-db-record-translate-field-names
put-db-record-translate-field-names.description: If true, the Processor will attempt to translate field names into the appropriate column names for the table specified. If false, the field names must match the column names exactly, or the column will not be updated

put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior.name: put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior
put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior.description: If an incoming record has a field that does not map to any of the database table's columns, this property specifies how to handle the situation

allowableValue.description: Any field in the document that cannot be mapped to a column in the database is ignored
If the document has any field that cannot be mapped to a column in the database, the FlowFile will be routed to the failure relationship

put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior.name: put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior
put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior.description: If an incoming record does not have a field mapping for all of the database table's columns, this property specifies how to handle the situation

allowableValue.description: Any column in the database that does not have a field in the document will be assumed to not be required.  No notification will be logged
Any column in the database that does not have a field in the document will be assumed to not be required.  A warning will be logged
A flow will fail if any column in the database that does not have a field in the document.  An error will be logged

put-db-record-update-keys.name: put-db-record-update-keys
put-db-record-update-keys.description: A comma-separated list of column names that uniquely identifies a row in the database for UPDATE statements. If the Statement Type is UPDATE and this property is not set, the table's Primary Keys are used. In this case, if no Primary Key exists, the conversion to SQL will fail if Unmatched Column Behaviour is set to FAIL. This property is ignored if the Statement Type is INSERT

put-db-record-field-containing-sql.name: put-db-record-field-containing-sql
put-db-record-field-containing-sql.description: If the Statement Type is 'SQL' (as set in the statement.type attribute), this field indicates which field in the record(s) contains the SQL statement to execute. The value of the field must be a single SQL statement. If the Statement Type is not 'SQL', this field is ignored.

put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements.name: put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements
put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements.description: If the Statement Type is 'SQL' (as set in the statement.type attribute), this field indicates whether to split the field value by a semicolon and execute each statement separately. If any statement causes an error, the entire set of statements will be rolled back. If the Statement Type is not 'SQL', this field is ignored.

put-db-record-quoted-identifiers.name: put-db-record-quoted-identifiers
put-db-record-quoted-identifiers.description: Enabling this option will cause all column names to be quoted, allowing you to use reserved words as column names in your tables.

put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers.name: put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers
put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers.description: Enabling this option will cause the table name to be quoted to support the use of special characters in the table name.

put-db-record-query-timeout.name: put-db-record-query-timeout
put-db-record-query-timeout.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL statement , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

rollback-on-failure.name: rollback-on-failure
rollback-on-failure.description: Specify how to handle error. By default (false), if an error occurs while processing a FlowFile, the FlowFile will be routed to 'failure' or 'retry' relationship based on error type, and processor can continue with next FlowFile. Instead, you may want to rollback currently processed FlowFiles and stop further processing immediately. In that case, you can do so by enabling this 'Rollback On Failure' property.  If enabled, failed FlowFiles will stay in the input relationship without penalizing it and being processed repeatedly until it gets processed successfully or removed by other means. It is important to set adequate 'Yield Duration' to avoid retrying too frequently.

table-schema-cache-size.name: table-schema-cache-size
table-schema-cache-size.description: Specifies how many Table Schemas should be cached

put-db-record-max-batch-size.name: put-db-record-max-batch-size
put-db-record-max-batch-size.description: Specifies maximum number of sql statements to be included in each batch sent to the database. Zero means the batch size is not limited, and all statements are put into a single batch which can cause high memory usage issues for a very large number of statements.

database-session-autocommit.name: database-session-autocommit
database-session-autocommit.description: The autocommit mode to set on the database connection being used. If set to false, the operation(s) will be explicitly committed or rolled back (based on success or failure respectively). If set to true, the driver/database automatically handles the commit/rollback. Setting this property to 'No value' will leave the database connection's autocommit mode unmodified.

put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior.description: If an incoming record has a field that does not map to any of the database table's columns, this property specifies how to handle the situation

allowableValue.description: Any field in the document that cannot be mapped to a column in the database is ignored
If the document has any field that cannot be mapped to a column in the database, the FlowFile will be routed to the failure relationship

put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior.name: put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior
put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior.description: If an incoming record does not have a field mapping for all of the database table's columns, this property specifies how to handle the situation

allowableValue.description: Any column in the database that does not have a field in the document will be assumed to not be required.  No notification will be logged
Any column in the database that does not have a field in the document will be assumed to not be required.  A warning will be logged
A flow will fail if any column in the database that does not have a field in the document.  An error will be logged

put-db-record-update-keys.name: put-db-record-update-keys
put-db-record-update-keys.description: A comma-separated list of column names that uniquely identifies a row in the database for UPDATE statements. In this case, if no Primary Key exists, the conversion to SQL will fail if Unmatched Column Behaviour is set to FAIL. This property is ignored if the Statement Type is INSERT

put-db-record-field-containing-sql.name: put-db-record-field-containing-sql
put-db-record-field-containing-sql.description: If the Statement Type is 'SQL' (as set in the statement.type attribute), this field indicates which field in the record(s) contains the SQL statement to execute. The value of the field must be a single SQL statement. If the Statement Type is not 'SQL', this field is ignored.

put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements.name: put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements
put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements.description: If the Statement Type is 'SQL' (as set in the statement.type attribute), this field indicates whether to split the field value by a semicolon and execute each statement separately. put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers.name: put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers
