sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

relationships.name: failure
relationships.description: SQL query execution failed. Incoming FlowFile will be penalized and routed to this relationship

relationships.name: success
relationships.description: Successfully created FlowFile from SQL query result set.

properties.SQL select query:
/* ===== THIẾT LẬP THÁNG ===== */
SET @monthkey = CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE(), '%Y%m') AS UNSIGNED);

INSERT INTO db_hdnd_qttt.qlnv_cbcc_danhgia_hdndtp_new_rt
(
    monthkey,
    `year`,
    loaicapcha,
    loaicap,
    iddv,
    donvi,
    tenviettat,
    canbo_id,
    canbo_hoten,
    account,
		canbo_chuc_danh,
		canbo_chuc_vu,

    diem_danhgia,
    diem_chinhtritutuong,
    diem_nanglucvakynang,
    diem_nhiemvu,

    tongso,
    daht,
    daht_dh,
    daht_qh,
    daht_kh,

    dangth,
    dangth_th,
    dangth_qh,
    dangth_sqh,
    dangth_kh,

    tyle_hoanthanh,

    diem_tc01,
    diem_tc02,
    diem_tc03,
    diem_tc04,
    diem_tc05,
    diem_tc06,

    xeploai,
    xeploai_loaidanhgia
)

SELECT
    main.monthkey,
    main.`year`,
    main.loaicapcha,
    main.loaicap,
    main.iddv,
    main.donvi,
    main.tenviettat,
    main.canbo_id,
    main.canbo_hoten,
    main.account,
		main.canbo_chuc_danh,
		main.canbo_chuc_vu,
		

    main.diem_danhgia,
    main.diem_chinhtritutuong,
    main.diem_nanglucvakynang,
    main.diem_nhiemvu,

    main.tongso,
    main.daht,
    main.daht_dh,
    main.daht_qh,
    main.daht_kh,

    main.dangth,
    main.dangth_th,
    main.dangth_qh,
    main.dangth_sqh,
    main.dangth_kh,

    main.tyle_hoanthanh,

    main.diem_tc01,
    main.diem_tc02,
    main.diem_tc03,
    main.diem_tc04,
    main.diem_tc05,
    main.diem_tc06,

    CASE
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia IS NULL THEN 'Chưa có nhiệm vụ'
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia >= 90 THEN 'Hoàn thành xuất sắc nhiệm vụ'
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia >= 70 THEN 'Hoàn thành tốt nhiệm vụ'
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia >= 50 THEN 'Hoàn thành nhiệm vụ'
        ELSE 'Không hoàn thành nhiệm vụ'
    END AS xeploai,

    CASE
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia IS NULL THEN 'Chưa đánh giá'
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia >= 90 THEN 'Loại A'
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia >= 70 THEN 'Loại B'
        WHEN main.diem_danhgia >= 50 THEN 'Loại C'
        ELSE 'Loại D'
    END AS xeploai_loaidanhgia

FROM
(

SELECT
    m.monthkey,
    LEFT(m.monthkey,4) AS `year`,

    u.loaicapcha,
    u.loaicap,
    u.iddv,
    u.donvi,
    u.tenviettat,

    u.canbo_id,
    u.canbo_hoten,
    u.account,
		u.canbo_chuc_danh,
		u.canbo_chuc_vu,

    /* ===== điểm ===== */

    ROUND(
        (
            SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_dh,0)) +
            SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_qh,0))*0.75
        ) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100
    ,2) AS diem_danhgia,

    20 AS diem_chinhtritutuong,
    20 AS diem_nanglucvakynang,

    CASE
        WHEN SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)) = 0 THEN 60
        ELSE ROUND(
            (SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) /
            NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100) * 0.6
        ,2)
    END AS diem_nhiemvu,

    /* ===== thống kê ===== */

    SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)) AS tongso,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) AS daht,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_dh,0)) AS daht_dh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_qh,0)) AS daht_qh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_kh,0)) AS daht_kh,

    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth,0)) AS dangth,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_th,0)) AS dangth_th,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_qh,0)) AS dangth_qh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_sqh,0)) AS dangth_sqh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_kh,0)) AS dangth_kh,

    ROUND(
        SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) /
        NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100
    ,2) AS tyle_hoanthanh,

    NULL AS diem_tc01,
    NULL AS diem_tc02,
    NULL AS diem_tc03,
    NULL AS diem_tc04,
    NULL AS diem_tc05,
    NULL AS diem_tc06

FROM
(
    /* ===== danh sách tháng ===== */
    SELECT DISTINCT monthkey
    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan_new_rt
    WHERE monthkey <= @monthkey
) m

CROSS JOIN
(
    /* ===== danh sách cán bộ từ dm_user ===== */
    SELECT
        canbo_id,
        canbo_hoten,
        account,
        loaicapcha,
        loaicap,
        iddv,
        donvi,
        tenviettat,
				canbo_chuc_danh,
				canbo_chuc_vu
    FROM datamart_hanoi.dm_user
    WHERE loaicapcha = 'HĐND Thành phố'
    AND loaicap <> 'HĐND Xã, Phường'
) u

LEFT JOIN
(
    /* ===== dữ liệu nhiệm vụ ===== */

    SELECT
        t.monthkey,
        t.NguoiThucHienID AS canbo_id,

        COUNT(*) AS tongso,

        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Đã hoàn thành%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht_dh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht_qh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành không hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht_kh,

        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Chưa hoàn thành%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_th,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_qh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_sqh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành không hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_kh

    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan_new_rt t

    WHERE t.NguoiThucHienID IS NOT NULL
    AND t.loaicapcha = 'HĐND Thành phố'
    AND t.loaicap <> 'HĐND Xã, Phường'

    GROUP BY
        t.monthkey,
        t.NguoiThucHienID

) t

ON t.canbo_id = u.canbo_id
AND t.monthkey <= m.monthkey

WHERE m.monthkey <= @monthkey

GROUP BY
    m.monthkey,
    u.canbo_id

) main

ORDER BY
    main.monthkey,
    main.canbo_id

ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE

loaicapcha = VALUES(loaicapcha),
loaicap = VALUES(loaicap),
iddv = VALUES(iddv),
donvi = VALUES(donvi),
tenviettat = VALUES(tenviettat),

canbo_hoten = VALUES(canbo_hoten),

Database Connection Pooling Service.name: Database Connection Pooling Service
Database Connection Pooling Service.description: The Controller Service that is used to obtain connection to database

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

/* ===== THIẾT LẬP THÁNG ===== */
/* SET @monthkey = 202603;  */
SET @monthkey = CAST(DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE(), '%Y%m') AS UNSIGNED);


INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_cbcc_danhgia
(
    monthkey,
    year,
    loaicapcha,
    loaicap,
    iddv,
    donvi,
    tenviettat,
    canbo_id,
    canbo_hoten,
    account,

    diem_danhgia,
    diem_chinhtritutuong,
    diem_nanglucvakynang,
    diem_nhiemvu,

    tongso,
    daht,
    daht_dh,
    daht_qh,
    daht_kh,

    dangth,
    dangth_th,
    dangth_qh,
    dangth_sqh,
    dangth_kh,

    tyle_hoanthanh,

    diem_tc01,
    diem_tc02,
    diem_tc03,
    diem_tc04,
    diem_tc05,
    diem_tc06,

    xeploai,
    syncdate
)
SELECT
    m.monthkey,
    LEFT(m.monthkey,4) AS `year`,
    u.loaicapcha,
    u.loaicap,
    u.iddv,
    u.donvi,
    u.tenviettat,

    u.canbo_id,
    u.canbo_hoten,
    u.account,

    /* ===== điểm ===== */
    (ROUND((SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100) * 0.6,2) + 40) AS diem_danhgia,

    20 AS diem_chinhtritutuong,
    20 AS diem_nanglucvakynang,

    ROUND((SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100) * 0.6,2) AS diem_nhiemvu,

    SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)) AS tongso,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) AS daht,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_dh,0)) AS daht_dh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_qh,0)) AS daht_qh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.daht_kh,0)) AS daht_kh,

    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth,0)) AS dangth,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_th,0)) AS dangth_th,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_qh,0)) AS dangth_qh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_sqh,0)) AS dangth_sqh,
    SUM(IFNULL(t.dangth_kh,0)) AS dangth_kh,

    ROUND(
        SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100
    ,2) AS tyle_hoanthanh,

    NULL AS diem_tc01,
    NULL AS diem_tc02,
    NULL AS diem_tc03,
    NULL AS diem_tc04,
    NULL AS diem_tc05,
    NULL AS diem_tc06,

    CASE
        WHEN (ROUND((SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100) * 0.6,2) + 40) >= 90
            THEN 'Hoàn thành xuất sắc nhiệm vụ'
        WHEN (ROUND((SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100) * 0.6,2) + 40) >= 70
            THEN 'Hoàn thành tốt nhiệm vụ'
        WHEN (ROUND((SUM(IFNULL(t.daht,0)) / NULLIF(SUM(IFNULL(t.tongso,0)),0) * 100) * 0.6,2) + 40) >= 50
            THEN 'Hoàn thành nhiệm vụ'
        ELSE 'Không hoàn thành nhiệm vụ'
    END AS xeploai,

    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM
(
    /* ===== calendar month ===== */
    SELECT DISTINCT monthkey
    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan
    WHERE monthkey <= @monthkey
) m

CROSS JOIN
(
    /* ===== danh sách cán bộ ===== */
    SELECT DISTINCT
        t.NguoiThucHienID AS canbo_id,
        u.FullName AS canbo_hoten,
        u.Username AS account,
        t.loaicapcha,
        t.loaicap,
        t.iddv,
        t.donvi,
        t.tenviettat
    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan t
    LEFT JOIN egov_hanoi.`user` u
        ON u.UserId = t.NguoiThucHienID
    WHERE t.NguoiThucHienID IS NOT NULL
) u

LEFT JOIN
(
    /* ===== số liệu tháng ===== */
    SELECT
        t.monthkey,
        t.NguoiThucHienID AS canbo_id,

        COUNT(*) AS tongso,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Đã hoàn thành%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht_dh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht_qh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành không hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS daht_kh,

        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai LIKE 'Chưa hoàn thành%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_th,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_qh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_sqh,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành không hạn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dangth_kh

    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan t
    WHERE t.NguoiThucHienID IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
        t.monthkey,
        t.NguoiThucHienID
) t

ON t.canbo_id = u.canbo_id
AND t.monthkey <= m.monthkey

WHERE m.monthkey <= @monthkey

GROUP BY
    m.monthkey,
    u.canbo_id

ORDER BY
    m.monthkey,
    u.canbo_id
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

    -- Đã xác nhận canbo_id unique trong phạm vi lọc này -> không cần khử trùng
    SELECT canbo_id, donvi, canbo_hoten, canbo_chuc_danh
    FROM datamart_hanoi.dm_user
    WHERE loaicapcha        = 'UBND Thành phố'
      AND loaicap IS NULL
      AND canbo_chuc_danh LIKE '%Chủ tịch%'
) u
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT *
    FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task
    WHERE DeletedDate IS NULL
      AND (TargetDepartment IS NULL
           OR TargetDepartment NOT IN ('490.698','490.698.1307','490.698.1310','490.698.1841'))
) t
    ON u.canbo_id = t.AssignUser
INNER JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution r
    ON t.ResolutionId = r.ResolutionId
LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task_topic tp
    ON t.TopicId = tp.TopicId
   AND tp.DeletedDate IS NULL
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT TaskId, 'Chờ duyệt' AS nhiem_vu_cho_duyet
    FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_report
    WHERE Type IN (1, 2, 3, 4)
      AND Status = 0
    GROUP BY TaskId
) rp
    ON t.TaskId = rp.TaskId;

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

    NOW()                                               AS syncdate

    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan_new_rt
    WHERE loaicapcha_dvgiao = 'UBND Thành phố'
    GROUP BY Ma
) ct
    ON t.tt = ct.Ma;

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

Batch Size.name: Batch Size
Batch Size.description: The number of FlowFiles to be transferred in each invocation

Data Format.name: Data Format
Data Format.description: Specifies whether the data should be Text or Binary

Unique FlowFiles.name: Unique FlowFiles
Unique FlowFiles.description: If true, each FlowFile that is generated will be unique. If false, a random value will be generated and all FlowFiles will get the same content but this offers much higher throughput

generate-ff-custom-text.name: generate-ff-custom-text

Finally, if Expression Language is used, evaluation will be performed only once per batch of generated FlowFiles

mime-type.name: mime-type

put-db-record-dcbp-service.name: put-db-record-dcbp-service
put-db-record-dcbp-service.description: The Controller Service that is used to obtain a connection to the database for sending records.

put-db-record-catalog-name.description: The name of the catalog that the statement should update. This may not apply for the database that you are updating. In this case, leave the field empty. Note that if the property is set and the database is case-sensitive, the catalog name must match the database's catalog name exactly.

put-db-record-schema-name.name: put-db-record-schema-name
put-db-record-schema-name.description: The name of the schema that the table belongs to. This may not apply for the database that you are updating. In this case, leave the field empty. Note that if the property is set and the database is case-sensitive, the schema name must match the database's schema name exactly.

put-db-record-table-name.name: put-db-record-table-name
put-db-record-table-name.description: The name of the table that the statement should affect. Note that if the database is case-sensitive, the table name must match the database's table name exactly.

put-db-record-binary-format.name: put-db-record-binary-format
put-db-record-binary-format.description: The format to be applied when decoding string values to binary.

put-db-record-translate-field-names.name: put-db-record-translate-field-names

put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior.name: put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior
put-db-record-unmatched-field-behavior.description: If an incoming record has a field that does not map to any of the database table's columns, this property specifies how to handle the situation

allowableValue.description: Any field in the document that cannot be mapped to a column in the database is ignored

put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior.name: put-db-record-unmatched-column-behavior

allowableValue.description: Any column in the database that does not have a field in the document will be assumed to not be required.  No notification will be logged
Any column in the database that does not have a field in the document will be assumed to not be required.  A warning will be logged
A flow will fail if any column in the database that does not have a field in the document.  An error will be logged

put-db-record-field-containing-sql.name: put-db-record-field-containing-sql
put-db-record-field-containing-sql.description: If the Statement Type is 'SQL' (as set in the statement.type attribute), this field indicates which field in the record(s) contains the SQL statement to execute. The value of the field must be a single SQL statement. If the Statement Type is not 'SQL', this field is ignored.

put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements.name: put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements
put-db-record-allow-multiple-statements.description: If the Statement Type is 'SQL' (as set in the statement.type attribute), this field indicates whether to split the field value by a semicolon and execute each statement separately. If any statement causes an error, the entire set of statements will be rolled back. If the Statement Type is not 'SQL', this field is ignored.

put-db-record-quoted-identifiers.name: put-db-record-quoted-identifiers
put-db-record-quoted-identifiers.description: Enabling this option will cause all column names to be quoted, allowing you to use reserved words as column names in your tables.

put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers.name: put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers
put-db-record-quoted-table-identifiers.description: Enabling this option will cause the table name to be quoted to support the use of special characters in the table name.

put-db-record-query-timeout.name: put-db-record-query-timeout
put-db-record-query-timeout.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL statement , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

rollback-on-failure.name: rollback-on-failure
rollback-on-failure.description: Specify how to handle error. By default (false), if an error occurs while processing a FlowFile, the FlowFile will be routed to 'failure' or 'retry' relationship based on error type, and processor can continue with next FlowFile. Instead, you may want to rollback currently processed FlowFiles and stop further processing immediately. In that case, you can do so by enabling this 'Rollback On Failure' property.  If enabled, failed FlowFiles will stay in the input relationship without penalizing it and being processed repeatedly until it gets processed successfully or removed by other means. It is important to set adequate 'Yield Duration' to avoid retrying too frequently.

table-schema-cache-size.name: table-schema-cache-size
table-schema-cache-size.description: Specifies how many Table Schemas should be cached

put-db-record-max-batch-size.name: put-db-record-max-batch-size
put-db-record-max-batch-size.description: Specifies maximum number of sql statements to be included in each batch sent to the database. Zero means the batch size is not limited, and all statements are put into a single batch which can cause high memory usage issues for a very large number of statements.

database-session-autocommit.name: database-session-autocommit
database-session-autocommit.description: The autocommit mode to set on the database connection being used. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming FlowFile is expected to contain a valid SQL statement, to be issued by the processor to the database.

Support Fragmented Transactions.name: Support Fragmented Transactions
Support Fragmented Transactions.description: If true, when a FlowFile is consumed by this Processor, the Processor will first check the fragment.identifier and fragment.count attributes of that FlowFile. If the fragment.count value is greater than 1, the Processor will not process any FlowFile with that fragment.identifier until all are available; at that point, it will process all FlowFiles with that fragment.identifier as a single transaction, in the order specified by the FlowFiles' fragment.index attributes. This Provides atomicity of those SQL statements. Once any statement of this transaction throws exception when executing, this transaction will be rolled back. When transaction rollback happened, none of these FlowFiles would be routed to 'success'. If the <Rollback On Failure> is set true, these FlowFiles will stay in the input relationship. When the <Rollback On Failure> is set false,, if any of these FlowFiles will be routed to 'retry', all of these FlowFiles will be routed to 'retry'.Otherwise, they will be routed to 'failure'. If this value is false, these attributes will be ignored and the updates will occur independent of one another.

database-session-autocommit.name: database-session-autocommit
database-session-autocommit.description: The autocommit mode to set on the database connection being used. If set to false, the operation(s) will be explicitly committed or rolled back (based on success or failure respectively), if set to true the driver/database handles the commit/rollback.

Transaction Timeout.name: Transaction Timeout
Transaction Timeout.description: If the <Support Fragmented Transactions> property is set to true, specifies how long to wait for all FlowFiles for a particular fragment.identifier attribute to arrive before just transferring all of the FlowFiles with that identifier to the 'failure' relationship

Batch Size.name: Batch Size
Batch Size.description: The preferred number of FlowFiles to put to the database in a single transaction

Obtain Generated Keys.name: Obtain Generated Keys
Obtain Generated Keys.description: If true, any key that is automatically generated by the database will be added to the FlowFile that generated it using the sql.generate.key attribute. This may result in slightly slower performance and is not supported by all databases.

rollback-on-failure.name: rollback-on-failure

By default (false), if an error occurs while processing a FlowFile, the FlowFile will be routed to 'failure' or 'retry' relationship based on error type, and processor can continue with next FlowFile. Instead, you may want to rollback currently processed FlowFiles and stop further processing immediately. In that case, you can do so by enabling this 'Rollback On Failure' property.  If enabled, failed FlowFiles will stay in the input relationship without penalizing it and being processed repeatedly until it gets processed successfully or removed by other means. It is important to set adequate 'Yield Duration' to avoid retrying too frequently.

properties.SQL select query:
-- TRUNCATE TABLE datamart_hanoi.qlnv_kl_ctpct_chitiet;
-- INSERT INTO datamart_hanoi.qlnv_kl_ctpct_chitiet
SELECT
    NULL AS tt,
    r.DocCode AS so_ky_hieu,
    r.StartDate AS ngay_ban_hanh,
    r.Compendium AS trich_yeu,

    u.donvi AS phong_tham_muu,
    u.canbo_hoten AS nguoi_soan_thao,

    t.Title AS noi_dung_nhiem_vu,
		ct.LinhVuc AS linh_vuc,

    u.donvi AS don_vi_chu_tri,

    t.ExpireDate AS thoi_han,

    CASE 
			WHEN t.ExpireDate IS NULL THEN
				"Thường xuyên"
			ELSE
				ct.TrangThai
		END AS tinh_trang,

    NULL AS ket_qua_thuc_hien,

    t.UpdatedDate AS ngay_cap_nhat,

    u.canbo_hoten AS dau_moi_cap_nhat,

    u.canbo_chuc_danh AS chuc_danh,

    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM (
    SELECT *
    FROM datamart_hanoi.dm_user
    WHERE loaicapcha = 'UBND Thành phố'
			AND loaicap IS NULL
      AND canbo_chuc_danh LIKE '%Chủ tịch%'
) u
INNER JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution r
    ON u.canbo_id = r.CreateUser
INNER JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task t
    ON t.ResolutionId = r.ResolutionId
LEFT JOIN datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan ct
    ON t.TaskId = ct.Ma

The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

SELECT
    t.tt                                                AS tt,
    t.so_ky_hieu                                        AS so_ky_hieu,
    t.ngay_ban_hanh                                     AS ngay_ban_hanh,
    t.trich_yeu                                         AS trich_yeu,
    t.phong_tham_muu                                    AS phong_tham_muu,
    COALESCE(ct.NguoiTaoNhiemVu, t.nguoi_soan_thao)     AS nguoi_soan_thao,
    t.noi_dung_nhiem_vu                                 AS noi_dung_nhiem_vu,
    ct.DonViChuTri                                      AS don_vi_chu_tri,
    t.thoi_han                                          AS thoi_han,
    CASE
        WHEN ct.Ma IS NULL                                  THEN 'Chưa có báo cáo'
        WHEN ct.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn'        THEN 'Đã hoàn thành đúng hạn'
        WHEN ct.TrangThai = 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn'         THEN 'Đã hoàn thành quá hạn'
        WHEN ct.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn'     THEN 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn'
        WHEN ct.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành sắp quá hạn'   THEN 'Chưa hoàn thành trong hạn'
        WHEN ct.TrangThai = 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn'       THEN 'Chưa hoàn thành quá hạn'
        ELSE ct.TrangThai
    END                                                 AS tinh_trang,
    ''                                                  AS ket_qua_thuc_hien,
    t.ngay_cap_nhat                                     AS ngay_cap_nhat,
    COALESCE(ct.NguoiTaoNhiemVu, t.dau_moi_cap_nhat)    AS dau_moi_cap_nhat,
    t.chuc_danh                                         AS chuc_danh,
    ct.NguoiTaoNhiemVu                                  AS nguoi_tao_nhiem_vu,
    ct.donvi_dvtaonv                                    AS don_vi_nguoi_tao_nhiem_vu,
    t.dau_moi_cap_nhat                                  AS nguoi_giao_nhiem_vu,
    ct.Kieu                                             AS loai_van_ban,
    ct.LinhVuc                                          AS linh_vuc,
    t.chu_de                                            AS chu_de,
    t.nv_quantam                                        AS nv_quantam,
    t.nhiem_vu_cho_duyet                                AS nhiem_vu_cho_duyet,
    t.muc_do_uu_tien                                    AS muc_do_uu_tien,
    NOW()                                               AS syncdate
FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_kl_ctpct_chitiet_stage01_new_rt t
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        Ma,
        MAX(NguoiTaoNhiemVu)    AS NguoiTaoNhiemVu,
        MAX(DonViChuTri)        AS DonViChuTri,
        MAX(TrangThai)          AS TrangThai,
        MAX(donvi_dvtaonv)      AS donvi_dvtaonv,
        MAX(Kieu)               AS Kieu,
        MAX(LinhVuc)            AS LinhVuc
    FROM datamart_hanoi.qlnv_tonghop_chitiet_tiepnhan_new_rt
    WHERE loaicapcha_dvgiao = 'UBND Thành phố'
    GROUP BY Ma
) ct
    ON t.tt = ct.Ma;

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming FlowFiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming FlowFile is expected to contain a valid SQL statement, to be issued by the processor to the database.

Support Fragmented Transactions.name: Support Fragmented Transactions
Support Fragmented Transactions.description: If true, when a FlowFile is consumed by this Processor, the Processor will first check the fragment.identifier and fragment.count attributes of that FlowFile. If the fragment.count value is greater than 1, the Processor will not process any FlowFile with that fragment.identifier until all are available; at that point, it will process all FlowFiles with that fragment.identifier as a single transaction, in the order specified by the FlowFiles' fragment.index attributes. This Provides atomicity of those SQL statements. Once any statement of this transaction throws exception when executing, this transaction will be rolled back. When transaction rollback happened, none of these FlowFiles would be routed to 'success'. If the <Rollback On Failure> is set true, these FlowFiles will stay in the input relationship. When the <Rollback On Failure> is set false,, if any of these FlowFiles will be routed to 'retry', all of these FlowFiles will be routed to 'retry'.Otherwise, they will be routed to 'failure'. If this value is false, these attributes will be ignored and the updates will occur independent of one another.

database-session-autocommit.name: database-session-autocommit

Transaction Timeout.name: Transaction Timeout
Transaction Timeout.description: If the <Support Fragmented Transactions> property is set to true, specifies how long to wait for all FlowFiles for a particular fragment.identifier attribute to arrive before just transferring all of the FlowFiles with that identifier to the 'failure' relationship

Batch Size.name: Batch Size
Batch Size.description: The preferred number of FlowFiles to put to the database in a single transaction

Obtain Generated Keys.name: Obtain Generated Keys
Obtain Generated Keys.description: If true, any key that is automatically generated by the database will be added to the FlowFile that generated it using the sql.generate.key attribute. This may result in slightly slower performance and is not supported by all databases.

Instead, you may want to rollback currently processed FlowFiles and stop further processing immediately. In that case, you can do so by enabling this 'Rollback On Failure' property.  If enabled, failed FlowFiles will stay in the input relationship without penalizing it and being processed repeatedly until it gets processed successfully or removed by other means. It is important to set adequate 'Yield Duration' to avoid retrying too frequently.

    u.canbo_hoten AS nguoi_soan_thao,
    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS nguoi_tao_nhiem_vu,
    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS don_vi_nguoi_tao_nhiem_vu,
    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS loai_van_ban,

    r.Compendium AS noi_dung_nhiem_vu,
    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS linh_vuc,
    tp.TopicName AS chu_de,
    t.isFocus AS nv_quantam,
    rp.nhiem_vu_cho_duyet,

    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS don_vi_chu_tri,

    t.ExpireDate AS thoi_han,

    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS tinh_trang,
    CAST(NULL AS CHAR(255)) AS ket_qua_thuc_hien,

    t.UpdatedDate AS ngay_cap_nhat,

    u.canbo_hoten AS dau_moi_cap_nhat,

    u.canbo_chuc_danh AS chuc_danh,
    CASE 
        WHEN t.Priority = 3 THEN 'Hỏa tốc'
        WHEN t.Priority = 2 THEN 'Thượng khẩn'
        WHEN t.Priority = 1 THEN 'Khẩn'
        ELSE 'Thường'
    END AS muc_do_uu_tien,

    NOW() AS syncdate

FROM (
    SELECT *
    FROM datamart_hanoi.dm_user
    WHERE loaicapcha = 'UBND Thành phố'
      AND loaicap IS NULL
      AND canbo_chuc_danh LIKE '%Chủ tịch%'
) u
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT * 
    FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task 
    WHERE DeletedDate IS NULL 
      AND TargetDepartment NOT IN ('490.698', '490.698.1307', '490.698.1310', '490.698.1841')
) t
    ON u.canbo_id = t.AssignUser
INNER JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_resolution r
    ON t.ResolutionId = r.ResolutionId
LEFT JOIN db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_task_topic tp
    ON t.TopicId = tp.TopicId
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT TaskId, 'Chờ duyệt' AS nhiem_vu_cho_duyet
    FROM db_theodoinv_hn.qlnv_report
    WHERE Type IN (1, 2, 3, 4)
      AND Status = 0
) rp 
    ON t.TaskId = rp.TaskId;
/* đổi chỗ nguyên tử, chờ khóa tối đa 10s */
SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 10;

SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 31536000;

Database Connection Pooling Service.name: Database Connection Pooling Service
Database Connection Pooling Service.description: The Controller Service that is used to obtain connection to database

sql-pre-query.name: sql-pre-query
sql-pre-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed before the main SQL query is executed. For example, set session properties before main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

SQL select query.name: SQL select query
SQL select query.description: The SQL select query to execute. The query can be empty, a constant value, or built from attributes using Expression Language. If this property is specified, it will be used regardless of the content of incoming flowfiles. If this property is empty, the content of the incoming flow file is expected to contain a valid SQL select query, to be issued by the processor to the database. Note that Expression Language is not evaluated for flow file contents.

sql-post-query.name: sql-post-query
sql-post-query.description: A semicolon-delimited list of queries executed after the main SQL query is executed. Example like setting session properties after main query. It's possible to include semicolons in the statements themselves by escaping them with a backslash ('\;'). Results/outputs from these queries will be suppressed if there are no errors.

Max Wait Time.name: Max Wait Time
Max Wait Time.description: The maximum amount of time allowed for a running SQL select query  , zero means there is no limit. Max time less than 1 second will be equal to zero.

dbf-normalize.name: dbf-normalize
dbf-normalize.description: Whether to change non-Avro-compatible characters in column names to Avro-compatible characters. For example, colons and periods will be changed to underscores in order to build a valid Avro record.

dbf-user-logical-types.name: dbf-user-logical-types
dbf-user-logical-types.description: Whether to use Avro Logical Types for DECIMAL/NUMBER, DATE, TIME and TIMESTAMP columns. If disabled, written as string. If enabled, Logical types are used and written as its underlying type, specifically, DECIMAL/NUMBER as logical 'decimal': written as bytes with additional precision and scale meta data, DATE as logical 'date-millis': written as int denoting days since Unix epoch (1970-01-01), TIME as logical 'time-millis': written as int denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch, and TIMESTAMP as logical 'timestamp-millis': written as long denoting milliseconds since Unix epoch. If a reader of written Avro records also knows these logical types, then these values can be deserialized with more context depending on reader implementation.

compression-format.name: compression-format
compression-format.description: Compression type to use when writing Avro files. Default is None.

dbf-default-precision.name: dbf-default-precision
dbf-default-precision.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'precision' denoting number of available digits is required. Generally, precision is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However undefined precision (0) can be returned from some database engines. 'Default Decimal Precision' is used when writing those undefined precision numbers.

dbf-default-scale.name: dbf-default-scale
dbf-default-scale.description: When a DECIMAL/NUMBER value is written as a 'decimal' Avro logical type, a specific 'scale' denoting number of available decimal digits is required. Generally, scale is defined by column data type definition or database engines default. However when undefined precision (0) is returned, scale can also be uncertain with some database engines. 'Default Decimal Scale' is used when writing those undefined numbers. If a value has more decimals than specified scale, then the value will be rounded-up, e.g. 1.53 becomes 2 with scale 0, and 1.5 with scale 1.

esql-max-rows.name: esql-max-rows
esql-max-rows.description: The maximum number of result rows that will be included in a single FlowFile. This will allow you to break up very large result sets into multiple FlowFiles. If the value specified is zero, then all rows are returned in a single FlowFile.

esql-output-batch-size.name: esql-output-batch-size
esql-output-batch-size.description: The number of output FlowFiles to queue before committing the process session. When set to zero, the session will be committed when all result set rows have been processed and the output FlowFiles are ready for transfer to the downstream relationship. For large result sets, this can cause a large burst of FlowFiles to be transferred at the end of processor execution. If this property is set, then when the specified number of FlowFiles are ready for transfer, then the session will be committed, thus releasing the FlowFiles to the downstream relationship. NOTE: The fragment.count attribute will not be set on FlowFiles when this property is set.

esql-fetch-size.name: esql-fetch-size
esql-fetch-size.description: The number of result rows to be fetched from the result set at a time. This is a hint to the database driver and may not be honored and/or exact. If the value specified is zero, then the hint is ignored.

esql-auto-commit.name: esql-auto-commit
esql-auto-commit.description: Enables or disables the auto commit functionality of the DB connection. Default value is 'true'. The default value can be used with most of the JDBC drivers and this functionality doesn't have any impact in most of the cases since this processor is used to read data. However, for some JDBC drivers such as PostgreSQL driver, it is required to disable the auto committing functionality to limit the number of result rows fetching at a time. When auto commit is enabled, postgreSQL driver loads whole result set to memory at once. This could lead for a large amount of memory usage when executing queries which fetch large data sets. More Details of this behaviour in PostgreSQL driver can be found in https://jdbc.postgresql.org//documentation/head/query.html.

Attributes to Log.description: A comma-separated list of Attributes to Log. If not specified, all attributes will be logged unless `Attributes to Log by Regular Expression` is modified. There's an AND relationship between the two properties.

Attributes to Ignore.name: Attributes to Ignore
Attributes to Ignore.description: A comma-separated list of Attributes to ignore. If not specified, no attributes will be ignored unless `Attributes to Ignore by Regular Expression` is modified. There's an OR relationship between the two properties.

attributes-to-ignore-regex.name: attributes-to-ignore-regex

attributes-to-ignore-regex.description: A regular expression indicating the Attributes to Ignore. If not specified, no attributes will be ignored unless `Attributes to Ignore` is modified. There's an OR relationship between the two properties.

Log FlowFile Properties.name: Log FlowFile Properties
Log FlowFile Properties.description: Specifies whether or not to log FlowFile "properties", such as Entry Date, Lineage Start Date, and content size

allowableValue.description: Each FlowFile attribute will be logged using a single line for the attribute name and another line for the attribute value. This format is often most advantageous when looking at the attributes of a single FlowFile.
All FlowFile attribute names and values will be logged on a single line. This format is often most advantageous when comparing logs from multiple FlowFiles.
